issues.what: The study's primary reported finding, 'pre-registered null N1 rejected on 1 min: session memory beyond the hour effect, mean-reverting (+53..+106 INR/trade excess)', is a false positive produced by a mis-specified null, not evidence of memory. N1 fixes the SETUP positions and permutes outcomes within session x hour_bin cells, but the positions are generated by the outcomes: a Foundation trade runs until exit and the next SETUP can only occur after it (ledger identity asserted at session_stop.py:94-95; min gap exit->next SETUP = 1 bar), and winners hold ~6x longer than losers. So within a multi-member cell the early units are losers almost by construction and a long winner is the last unit; shuffling outcomes across fixed positions puts winners at rank 0, which the observed data almost never does, and the observed stat is mechanically above the permutation distribution in exactly the 'mean-reverting' direction. A process with ZERO memory reproduces every reported number.

issues.evidence: Real IS data (minute/L1, 4,452 units): l1 bars held win mean 110.6 (median 75.5) vs loss 18.7 (median 12.0), stop-loss exits 8.2; P(another unit follows in the session | win) 0.571 vs | loss 0.925; in multi-member session x hour cells the LAST unit wins 23.1% vs 1.5% for non-last units (rank-0 units 1.8%), mean net -595 vs -1,828; last unit of a multi-unit session wins 47.6% vs 10.2%. Simulation (scratchpad sim_memoryless.py, 2,000 draws, the study's own null_test/recompute_ledger/stats7 code): outcomes drawn iid within hour_bin from the real pool (no memory by construction), duration = the drawn unit's real duration, gaps from the empirical distribution, on the real 578-session skeleton -> seeds 11/22: units 4,624/4,542, all 7 tests reject N1 with Holm p <= 0.009, threshold excess +59..+118 INR/trade, Spearman excess -0.0216/-0.0203, last-in-cell win rate 0.248/0.240 vs 0.028/0.022 (real: excess +53..+106, Spearman -0.0233, Holm <= 0.014, 0.231 vs 0.015). Control variant with duration drawn independently of the outcome (seed 33): min Holm p 0.9025, excess -37..+32 (none significant), last-in-cell win rate 0.154 vs 0.147. The test therefore does not measure what DESIGN_PANEL:440 asks ('whether the causal session ledger predicts the next SETUP's net at all').
issues.fix: Re-word the result: 'N1 is rejected but the rejection is reproduced by a memoryless process with outcome-dependent trade duration; no session memory is shown'. Remove the 'mean-reverting memory' statement and the 'reverse rule' follow-up from FINDINGS.md / findings.json (or mark them as an artifact), and set session_memory_null_rejected to a value S49 will not read as memory. A valid test of ledger predictability must not condition on the realized within-session positions: e.g. compare net_j between ledger states within hour_bin across sessions (the hour_x_stops table already does this descriptively: +166/+73/+51/+132 in 09-12, -216/-289/-389 in 13-15) with a session-block bootstrap, or a simulation-based null that regenerates positions from durations. The no-key decision does not change.

issues.what: The reading 'every cell sits at the 0.0th control percentile: the rule does worse than picking the same number of same-session SETUPs at random' is the same artifact seen from the comparator side. The session-matched random control draws n_s of the N_s positions realized in the session, including the last ones, which are long winners by construction; N_s is only known at session end, so for a within-session sequential rule (which always keeps the earliest positions) the control is a hindsight-biased comparator, not a random implementable alternative. The design/Judge 1 asserted 'the standard control applies directly' (DESIGN_PANEL:442, :454); the study inherited that, but its interpretation of control_pct 0.0 as anti-edge is not supported.
issues.where: FINDINGS.md:186 ('The rule therefore does worse than picking the same number of same-session SETUPs at random in essentially every draw'), :215, :304; findings.json branch_b.grid[*].control_pct reading; harness.go_no_go check control_pct>=95 applied to a sequential rule (harness.py:568).
issues.evidence: On the memoryless simulated stream (no edge or anti-edge possible by construction) the k=2/L=None absorbing rule sits at session-matched control pct 0.0 with p_beat 1.0 in both seeds (pooled diff +34.1 / +20.7); with duration independent of outcome the same rule is at control pct 7.6. Real data: control pct 0.0 for all 32 cells.
issues.fix: Do not use control_pct as evidence for or against within-session sequential rules; judge them on the hindsight-free pooled kept-vs-skipped statistics only (nested OOF, CPCV, top-1%-removed, PBO), which in this study already fail (OOF diff -52.05, 6/12 blocks; CPCV median -30.93, p5 -80.12; diff_top1_removed -14.68; PBO 0.8392) and alone support 'no key'. Flag to the orchestrator that go_no_go's control check is uninformative for any sequential (position-order) rule.
